main_text.l: tanis consulentem dedisse iis geminam regum prosapiam, ex una stirpe descen-dentem, quod mediocritati congruen-tius: dein divino quodam consilio mo-deratam senum potestatem ἰσόψηφον[?], hoc est, æquipollentem in suffragiis, insolenti regum potestati fuisse adjun-ctam, atque eo modo, præsertim ad-dito etiam postea ad tumentem adhuc paucorum potentiam comprimendam ephororum magistratu, rempublicam maximè temperatam extitisse. Hæc potestas regum domi, perarcta sane, si cum iure aliorum regum conferatur.

Accedebat, quòd ὑβρισταί[?] etiam re-{*}ges essent, & ad judicia de ipsis constitu-tuta vocari, & , si criminum convince-rentur, sententiis judicum damnari pos-sent, salvo aliquo ad populum provo-candi jure. Atque hoc est, quod de iis Aristoteles in politicis ait, regnum in republ. Laconicâ maximè legibus astri-ctum videri: quodque Xenophon de consilio Lycurgi in fine libelli de republicâ Laconicâ scribit, tribuisse eum regibus domi agentibus honores modi-cos, non multum superantes modum privatorum: nec voluisse aut tyrannico sensu fastuve animos horum inflare, aut potestatis regiæ invidiam civibus inserere: attamen mortuos velut he-

page.notes: Greek ἰσόψηφον and ὑβρισταί are read from a small, worn print; both are doubtful. The asterisk before "ges" stands at the line start, and no matching note appears on the page. The curved stroke after "extitisse" and "inflare" is unclear and may be a tilde or a stray mark; the words are given as printed. At the bottom left, "fensi." and "aut jus / ens" are show-through from the reverse side and are omitted. The left edge fragments are not part of this page and are omitted. Long s has been rendered as s throughout.
